sculptory.setting.select.fill_with.toolt: What Fill and Walls write: the active block (the one in the top bar), or the weighted palette below.
sculptory.setting.select.palette.tooltip: The blocks Fill and Walls use and how often: each block's share is its weight (1 to 1000) over the total. Up to 16 blocks.
sculptory.setting.select.into.tooltip: Which blocks Fill writes: everything in the selection, only existing blocks (air stays air; water and plants count as blocks), or only air (what is there stays). Walls and Hollow always write everything. The Shape brush's Place, Air only and Paint modes are the same choice.
sculptory.setting.select.thickness.toolt: How many blocks thick Hollow's shell and the Walls are, 1 to 16. To hollow a box, it must be thicker than two walls.
sculptory.setting.select.entities.toolti: What Copy and Cut take along with the blocks: None, Decorations (item frames, paintings, armor stands, displays, minecarts, boats...) or Decorations and mobs. Players and dropped items never.
sculptory.setting.select.symmetry.toolti: Fill, Replace, Erase, Hollow and Walls also run on the mirrored or turned copies of the selection, around the symmetry centre set with the symmetry centre key (M by default; with Shift a block corner; the same point again clears it). Without a centre set the operation is refused: set one first.
sculptory.setting.select.mode.tooltip: Box: drag a box, or a shape inside it. Magic: click a block to select the connected blocks that match it (Shift+click adds, Alt+click removes). Brush: drag a sphere over blocks to add them (Alt+drag removes). Lasso: drag a loop on the ground to select what is inside it, some layers high (Shift adds, Alt removes).
sculptory.setting.select.brush_radius.to: The radius of the sphere the brush selects with, in blocks. Ctrl+Scroll changes it.
sculptory.setting.select.solid_only.tool: On: the brush adds only blocks that aren't air, and skips chunks your game hasn't loaded. Off: it adds every block of the sphere, air included.
sculptory.setting.select.lasso_height.to: How many layers the lasso selects, from the block you pressed on upward. Alt+Scroll changes it.
sculptory.setting.select.shape.tooltip: What the box you drag selects: the whole box, or the shape that fits inside it. Every operation works on exactly the shape's blocks. Changing it reshapes the current selection.
sculptory.setting.select.axis.tooltip: Which way the cylinder runs through its box
sculptory.setting.select.facing.tooltip: Where the tip of the cone or pyramid points; its base fills the opposite side of the box
sculptory.setting.select.match.tooltip: Same block: the clicked block in any state (every oak stair, whichever way it faces). Exact state: only blocks exactly like the clicked one. Any block: everything but air.
sculptory.setting.select.connect.tooltip: Faces: only blocks touching side to side. Diagonals too: also blocks touching at an edge or a corner.
sculptory.setting.select.limit.tooltip: Magic select stops after this many blocks, and says so. The server's edit limit caps it.
sculptory.setting.brush.radius.tooltip: How far the brush reaches from its centre, in blocks: 1 to 32, or less if the server sets a lower maximum. The brush is 2 × radius + 1 blocks across. Ctrl+Scroll changes it (Shift: steps of 4).
sculptory.setting.brush.strength.tooltip: How much each dab does, 0 to 1. Raise and Lower: that many blocks per dab at the centre. Smooth and Flatten: that share of the way to the target. Paint: below 1, a spot needs several dabs. Alt+Scroll changes it.
sculptory.setting.brush.falloff.tooltip: How the strength fades from the centre of the brush to its edge. The cursor's inner ring shows roughly where it starts to drop.
sculptory.setting.brush.falloff.constant: Full strength everywhere in the brush, right up to its edge.
sculptory.setting.brush.falloff.linear.t: Fades evenly, from full strength at the centre to none at the edge: half strength halfway out.
sculptory.setting.brush.falloff.smooth.t: Stays near full close to the centre, then eases out to none at the edge along an S-curve: half strength halfway out.
sculptory.setting.brush.falloff.sphere.t: Shaped like a dome: stays strong over most of the brush (87%% halfway out), then drops steeply to none at the edge.
sculptory.setting.brush.shape.tooltip: The brush's footprint on the ground: a circle, or a square as wide as the circle (in Surface mode a ball or a cube). The falloff fades toward its edge.
sculptory.setting.brush.shape.circle.too: The columns within the radius of the centre (in Surface mode the blocks within the radius: a ball). The strength fades with the distance from the centre.
sculptory.setting.brush.shape.square.too: The columns within the radius both east–west and north–south (in Surface mode up–down too: a cube). The strength fades toward the sides, so the corners are as weak as the middle of a side.
sculptory.setting.brush.mode.tooltip: How Raise, Lower, Smooth, Flatten and Weather work. Surface: on whatever you aim at, floors, walls and ceilings alike: Raise, Lower and Flatten inside a cylinder of the radius facing the surface, Smooth and Weather inside the ball. Terrain: each column of the ground moves up or down, as seen from above (Weather works on what the sky sees).
sculptory.setting.brush.mode.surface.too: Works on the surface you aim at, the way it faces: Raise pushes it out, Lower pulls it in, Smooth evens out bumps and dents, Flatten flattens to the face the stroke starts on. Raise, Lower and Flatten change only blocks inside a cylinder of the radius facing the surface; Smooth only those inside the ball.
sculptory.setting.brush.mode.terrain.too: Moves each column of the footprint up or down as a whole, as seen from above. Faster for big landscapes and never makes overhangs; walls and ceilings are left alone.
sculptory.setting.brush.weather.mode.too: What the Weather brush does to the surface it passes over.
sculptory.setting.brush.weather.mode.ero: Wears exposed blocks away: spikes and overhang lips first, then corners, then edges.
sculptory.setting.brush.weather.mode.fil: Fills holes, pits and cracks with the blocks around them.
sculptory.setting.brush.weather.mode.rou: Breaks a smooth surface up into lumps and dents (new ones each stroke).
sculptory.setting.brush.weather.mode.mel: Slumps steep edges down to 45 degrees and lets overhangs drip, moving blocks rather than removing them.
sculptory.setting.brush.material.tooltip: The block Paint puts on the surface, Layer depth blocks deep. Middle-click a block in the world to pick it.
sculptory.setting.brush.palette.tooltip: The blocks used and how often: each block's share is its weight (1 to 1000) over the total. Up to 64 blocks. Middle-click a block in the world to add it.
sculptory.setting.pattern.kind.tooltip: How the mix's blocks are laid out. The order of the mix (drag its rows by ≡) runs from first to last in Gradient and Steepness.
sculptory.setting.pattern.kind.random.to: Each block picked at random by weight: a speckled mix.
sculptory.setting.pattern.kind.patches.t: Blocks form natural clumps instead of speckle. The weights still set roughly how much of each block appears.
The mix fades from its first block to its last along a line: Alt+drag in the world to draw it. Each block takes a stretch by its weight.
sculptory.setting.pattern.kind.steepness: Flat ground gets the first block, the steepest faces the last, the others in between (grass on flats, stone on cliffs).
sculptory.setting.pattern.steepness_unav: Steepness works only in Palette Paint: it paints by the slope of the ground around each column.
sculptory.setting.pattern.size.tooltip: About how many blocks across each patch is, 1 to 32.
sculptory.setting.pattern.edge.tooltip: How many blocks wide the dithered blend between two blocks is, 0 (a hard line) to 32.
sculptory.setting.pattern.steepness_edge: How ragged the change from one block to the next is, in degrees of slope, 0 (a hard line) to 45.
sculptory.setting.pattern.seed.tooltip: The same seed gives the same pattern every time. Re-roll for another one.
sculptory.setting.brush.depth.tooltip: How many blocks down from the surface Paint and Palette Paint repaint, 1 to 32. It stops early where the ground ends (air, water, stairs, chests and the like).
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.blocks: Only on these surface blocks (empty: any)
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.blocks.tool: Brush only where the top ground block is one of these (in Surface mode: the surface block that moves, or the block a smoothed block takes or loses); grass, flowers and water above it are looked through. Up to 16 blocks; empty: anywhere.
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.y.tooltip: Brush only where the top ground block's height is in this range (in Surface mode: the height of each block that changes). The full range, -64 to 319, means no limit.
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.slope.toolt: Brush only where the steepest step from the surface to a neighbouring column (north, south, east or west) is in this range, in blocks. In Surface mode: how steep the surface is at the block, in blocks up per block across (walls count as 16). The full range, 0 to 16, means no limit.
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.exact.toolt: On: only the exact states listed (a log's axis, a snowy grass block). Off: any state of the listed blocks.
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.invert.tool: Brush only where the blocks, height and slope limits above do not match. No effect while none of them is set.
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.selection.t: Change only blocks inside the selection box, as it is when the stroke starts. A shaped or block selection counts as the box around it. Invert mask does not flip it.
sculptory.notice.builder.masked: The mask keeps that block from changing (Ctrl+M turns the mask off)
sculptory.setting.brush.mask.rules.toolt: Rules the ground block a brush changes must pass (every rule must match; each can be flipped with Not). They are tested at the surface block, as the brush finds it. The global Mask (top bar, Ctrl+M) applies too: both must let a block through.
sculptory.mask.chip.tooltip.empty: Mask: limit every edit to the blocks you choose. Click to add rules; %s switches it on and off.
sculptory.mask.chip.tooltip.on: Mask on: edits change only blocks where %s. Click to edit; %s switches it off.
sculptory.mask.chip.tooltip.off: Mask off (%s). Click to edit; %s switches it on.
sculptory.mask.notice.on: Mask on: edits change only the blocks it lets through
sculptory.mask.notice.no_rules: The mask has no rules yet: add one in the Mask window
sculptory.mask.on.tooltip: While on, every edit (fills, pastes, brushes, builder mode, …) changes only the blocks every rule lets through. %s switches it too. Every game starts with it off.
sculptory.mask.about: Every rule must match. Each rule tests a block as it was before the edit; Move, Cut and Copy test where the blocks are taken from.
sculptory.mask.no_rules: No rules yet: the mask lets everything through.
sculptory.mask.add_rule.tooltip: Add a rule: the blocks an edit may change must pass it too
sculptory.mask.invert_all.tooltip: Brush only where the rules above do not all match (what Invert mask did before rules)
sculptory.mask.not.tooltip: Flip this rule: it matches where it would not
sculptory.mask.reroll.tooltip: Another random pattern with the same share of blocks
sculptory.mask.inside.about: Blocks inside the selection as it is when you edit. With nothing selected it matches no block.
sculptory.mask.blocks.tooltip: Blocks and block tags (up to 16). Click to change them.
sculptory.mask.warning.server: This server can't apply a mask: while it is on, edits here are refused. Turn it off to edit.
sculptory.mask.warning.no_selection: Nothing is selected: the Inside the selection rule matches no block.
sculptory.mask.warning.no_rules: The mask is on but has no rules: it lets everything through.
sculptory.notice.mask.no_server_support: The mask is on, but this server can't apply it: turn it off (Ctrl+M) to edit here
sculptory.notice.mask.sending: The mask's selection is still being sent to the server: try again in a moment
sculptory.notice.mask.refused: The server refused the mask (%s): edits wait until the mask changes
sculptory.picker.set.hint: Click adds a block or tag · # lists tags · type a state like oak_log[axis=y] and press Enter for an exact state
sculptory.setting.brush.symmetry.tooltip: Around the symmetry centre: the point set with the symmetry centre key (M by default; with Shift a block corner; the same point again clears it), otherwise the selection's centre. The centre and the mirror planes show in the world.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.tooltip: The solid placed at each click, or along a drag. All but the sphere use Height and Facing.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.sphere.tool: Round every way, 2 × radius + 1 blocks across. Height and Facing don't apply.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.cylinder.to: Round, 2 × radius + 1 blocks across, and Height long along its facing.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.cone.toolti: A round base 2 × radius + 1 blocks across, narrowing over Height to a tip at the facing end.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.cube.toolti: A square box, 2 × radius + 1 blocks wide and Height long along its facing: a true cube with Height = diameter.
sculptory.setting.shape.kind.pyramid.too: A square base 2 × radius + 1 blocks wide, narrowing over Height to a tip at the facing end.
sculptory.setting.shape.height_auto.tool: Off: set the height yourself (Alt+Scroll changes it)
sculptory.setting.shape.height.tooltip: The shape's length along its facing, in blocks: 1 to 65, or at most the largest diameter the server allows. Alt+Scroll changes it.
sculptory.setting.shape.facing.tooltip: The axis of a cylinder, the tip of a cone or pyramid, the long side of a cube. Clicked face: away from the face you click, so a click on a wall makes a horizontal cylinder.
sculptory.setting.shape.anchor.tooltip: Centre: the shape is centred on the block you click. On surface: it rests on the face you click, outside the block.

sculptory.setting.extrude.diagonals.tool: Blocks touching the face only at a corner join it too
sculptory.setting.extrude.size.tooltip: The face stops after this many blocks, and says so. The server's selection limit caps it.
sculptory.setting.extrude.max_layers.too: The most layers one drag pulls out or carves

sculptory.setting.generate.kind.tooltip: Path: a road along the nodes you click on the ground. Roof: a roof over the selection. Line: a line or curve through the blocks you click.
sculptory.setting.generate.width.tooltip: The road's width in blocks, 1 to 32. Ctrl+Scroll changes it (Shift: steps of 4). An even width is centred on a corner of the node's block.
sculptory.setting.generate.material.tool: What the road is paved with: one block, or a weighted mix of blocks.
sculptory.setting.generate.block.tooltip: The block the road is made of: its surface, and the blocks under it with Fill below.

sculptory.setting.generate.border.toolti: A second material for the outermost block on each side of the road

sculptory.setting.generate.height.toolti: Follow terrain: the road lies on the ground, smoothed along its length. Straight between points: the height runs straight from node to node, whatever the ground does.

sculptory.setting.generate.fill_below.to: Blocks of material written under the surface (an embankment); 0 for none
sculptory.setting.generate.clear_above.t: Blocks cleared to air above the surface; 0 for none
sculptory.setting.generate.style.tooltip: The roof's shape. Gable: two slopes meeting at a ridge. Hip: slopes on all four sides. Shed: one slope, rising from the Low side.
sculptory.setting.generate.style.gable.t: Two slopes meeting at a ridge, with triangular ends (Gable walls fills them).
sculptory.setting.generate.style.hip.too: Slopes on all four sides. The ridge runs along the longer side; a square roof comes to a point.
sculptory.setting.generate.style.shed.to: A single slope, rising from the Low side to the opposite side.
sculptory.setting.generate.ridge.tooltip: Which way a gable roof's ridge runs. Auto: along the longer side of the box, overhang included.
sculptory.setting.generate.low_side.tool: The side where a shed roof comes down to the eaves; it rises from there to the opposite side.
sculptory.setting.generate.pitch.tooltip: How steep the roof is, and so which of the three blocks it is made of.
One block up per block across, in stairs, with the full block on the ridge. The Slab isn't used.
sculptory.setting.generate.pitch.steep.t: Two blocks up per block across, all in the full block: no stairs or slabs.
Half a block up per block across: rows of slabs and full blocks in turn. The Stairs block isn't used.
sculptory.setting.generate.overhang.tool: How far the eaves reach past the selection box on every side, 0 to 4 blocks.
sculptory.setting.generate.thickness.too: Layers of the full block under the roof's surface
sculptory.setting.generate.gable_walls.t: Fill the triangular ends with the full block (a hip roof has none)
sculptory.setting.generate.inside.toolti: Hollow: clear the space under the roof inside the footprint, above the eaves
sculptory.setting.generate.stairs.toolti: Picking a stairs block fills the slab and full block when they derive from its name
sculptory.setting.generate.slab.tooltip: Used only at the Gentle pitch, for every other row of the slope.
sculptory.setting.generate.full.tooltip: The ridge row, the layers under the surface (Thickness), the gable walls, the whole slope at the Steep pitch and every other row at the Gentle one.
sculptory.setting.generate.line_path.too: How the line runs through its points. Straight: straight from point to point. Curve: a smooth curve through every point (last point on the first: a closed loop). Hanging: sags between each pair of points, like a rope or a cable.
sculptory.setting.generate.line_sag.tool: How far each span hangs below the straight line between its two points, at its middle, 0 to 64 blocks. A span straight up or down doesn't sag.
sculptory.setting.generate.line_thicknes: How thick the line is, 1 to 16 blocks. Ctrl+Scroll changes it (Shift: steps of 4). An even thickness runs half a block off the points' centres.
Round: a tube (3 across is a full 3 × 3, as the Shape brush's cylinders). Square: a square beam, level across.
sculptory.setting.generate.line_material: What the line is made of: one block, or a weighted mix of blocks.
sculptory.setting.generate.line_block.to: The block the line is made of
The line's blocks and how often: each block's share is its weight over the total. The same line built again gets the same pattern.

sculptory.setting.place.include_air: Include air (clears blocks where the clipboard has air)

sculptory.quick_start.find: Find any command, tool or setting
sculptory.quick_start.back: Step back: close, cancel, then leave
sculptory.quick_start.got_it.tooltip: Hide this card for good (Enter or Esc). Help > Quick start shows it again.

sculptory.tutorial.card.nothing_made: This lesson made no changes to your world.

sculptory.tutorial.card.undid_one: Undid the change this lesson made.

sculptory.tutorial.window.intro: Lessons run in your own world with the real tools. Each step ticks itself off when you do it.
sculptory.tutorial.window.resume.tooltip: Go on with the lesson at the step you left
sculptory.tutorial.window.restart.toolti: Click to do it again from its first step
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.getting_around: Look around, fly, change the fly speed, and leave the editor and come back.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.welcom: Lessons run in your own world with the real tools: do what this card says and each step ticks itself off. Back and Skip step move between steps; Exit pauses the lesson. At the end you can undo what a lesson built.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.look: %s to look around: hold the right mouse button and move the mouse. The cursor comes back where it was.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.move: Move with %s. In Creative, %s flies up and %s flies down. Press %s to jump onto the block under the cursor; %s goes through a wall.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.fly_sp: %s changes the fly speed, from 0.25× to 8×. The top bar shows it.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.esc: %s steps back one level at a time: it closes a menu, leaves a text field, cancels a drag, stroke or preview, and at last leaves the editor.
sculptory.tutorial.getting_around.leave: Press %s to leave the editor, then %s again to come back. The lesson waits for you.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.menus.summary: The menu bar, the command search, the key sheet, Notifications and the keyboard in windows.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.view_menu: Click View in the menu bar at the top. Every command is in one of these menus, with its key on the right.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.notifications: Click Notifications in the View menu: it lists the last messages the editor showed, so one you missed can be read again.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.search: Press %s and type a few letters, such as sym cen: the search finds every command, tool, setting and preset. Esc closes it again.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.key_sheet: Press %s for the key sheet: every key as you have it bound. Type to filter it, then press %s or Esc to close it.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.f6: Press %s to move the keyboard into a window: Tab moves within it, and Enter or Space presses a button.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.hide: Press %s to give the keyboard back, then %s to hide all windows. Press it again to show them.
sculptory.tutorial.menus.windows: Drag a window by its title bar and resize it from any edge. View > Reset layout puts every window back at its default place.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.select.summary: Draw a box, resize and nudge it, select shapes and connected blocks, and clear the selection.
sculptory.tutorial.select.pick: Press %s to pick the Select tool (or click it in the palette at the bottom).
sculptory.tutorial.select.box: Left-drag from one block to another to draw a box between them.
sculptory.tutorial.select.resize: Drag a face handle to move that face, or point at a face and use %s to grow or shrink it (hold Shift for steps of 4).
sculptory.tutorial.select.nudge: Nudge the box a block the way you face with %s, %s, %s and %s (hold Shift for 10); %s and %s move it up and down.
sculptory.tutorial.select.shape: In Tool Settings, set Shape to Sphere: your box now selects the sphere that fits inside it.
sculptory.tutorial.select.magic: Set Select by to Magic, then click a block: every block of that kind connected to it is selected.
sculptory.tutorial.select.box_again: Set Select by back to Box, and Shape back to Box.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.edit.summary: Fill, replace, copy, paste, move, stack and erase what you selected.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.box: Press %s and drag a box a few blocks across, somewhere you don't mind changing.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.block: Choose the block to build with: click the block in the top bar and pick one, or %s a block in the world.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.fill: Open the Selection menu and click Fill: the selection fills with that block. The Selection window has the same buttons.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.replace: Selection > Replace… turns one kind of block into another: pick From and To, then click Replace. Replace oak planks with spruce planks with Whole family on to re-wood a house: its oak stairs, slabs, fences and doors turn spruce too.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.paste: Press %s: a see-through copy follows the cursor. Click to drop it where you want it, then press %s to place it. If pasted fences or panes don't join their new neighbours, select them and use Selection > Update blocks.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.move: Selection > Move turns the selection into a ghost and marks its place in red. Put it somewhere else and press %s.
sculptory.tutorial.edit.stack: Selection > Stack repeats the selection: drag the first copy to set the step, %s sets how many copies, and %s stacks them.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.terrain.summar: Raise, Lower, Smooth and Flatten the ground, and set a brush's radius and strength.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.raise: Left-drag on the ground to push it up (a wall or a ceiling works too). One press is one undo step.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.radius: %s changes the brush's radius; the ring shows it. The Radius slider in Tool Settings does the same.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.strength: %s changes the strength: how much each dab does.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.lower: Press %s for Lower and dig a little. Holding Alt while you drag turns Raise into Lower, and Lower into Raise.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.smooth: Press %s for Smooth and brush over the bumps you made.
sculptory.tutorial.terrain.flatten: Press %s for Flatten: it levels to the face where your stroke starts, and keeps levelling while you hold the button.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.weather.summar: Wear the ground down, fill it in, roughen it or let it slump with the Weather brush.
sculptory.tutorial.weather.mode: Its Weather setting picks what it does: Erode wears edges and spikes away, Fill in fills holes and cracks, Roughen breaks a flat surface up, and Melt lets steep ground slump.
sculptory.tutorial.weather.erode_mode: Set Weather to Erode, if it isn't already.
sculptory.tutorial.weather.erode: With Erode, hold the button over a hill or a cliff edge: the brush keeps working while you hold it still.
sculptory.tutorial.weather.melt_stroke: Brush over a steep slope or a pillar: blocks slide and drop until nothing is steeper than 45°. Melt only moves blocks, it never makes or loses one.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.paint.summary: Repaint the ground with one block or a weighted mix, and limit a brush with a mask.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.material: %s a block in the world to make it the Material, or pick one in Tool Settings.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.paint: Left-drag on the ground to repaint its top blocks.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.palette_pick: Press %s for Palette Paint: it paints a weighted mix of blocks.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.mix: %s a block to add it to the mix, or change a block's weight in Tool Settings.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.palettes: Save palette… and Load palette…, above the settings, keep a mix in the server's library for everyone on it.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.mask: Open the Mask section in Tool Settings, click Edit… under Brush only where and add the rule Is one of these blocks with a surface block: the brush then works only where the surface is that block.
sculptory.tutorial.paint.mask_paint: Paint across it: only the surface blocks your rule names change. Remove the rule again when you're done.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.patterns.summa: Lay a mix out in patches, or along a line you draw, instead of at random.
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.pick: Press %s for Palette Paint and put two or three blocks in its mix (%s a block in the world adds it).
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.patches: In Tool Settings, set Pattern to Patches.
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.paint_patche: Paint: the blocks form clumps instead of speckle. Patch size sets how big they are; Re-roll gives another layout.
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.line: Alt+drag from one block to another in the world: the mix runs along that line, its first block at the start and its last at the end.
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.paint_gradie: Paint across the line. Drag the mix's rows by ≡ to change their order; Edge sets how wide the blends are.
sculptory.tutorial.patterns.others: Fill and the Shape brush take the same patterns, and a saved palette keeps its pattern. Steepness (Palette Paint only) puts the first block on flat ground and the last on cliffs.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.shapes.summary: Place spheres and cylinders with the Shape brush, and fill a shape you selected.
sculptory.tutorial.shapes.click: Click the ground to place a sphere of the block in the top bar. The outline shows exactly where it goes.
sculptory.tutorial.shapes.kind: In Tool Settings, set Shape to Cylinder.
sculptory.tutorial.shapes.drag: Now hold the button and drag along the ground: cylinders are laid along the way and merge into one smooth shape. A click, however long you hold it, places just one.
sculptory.tutorial.shapes.select_cone: Selections have shapes too: press %s, set Shape to Cone in Tool Settings and drag a box. The cone fills it.
sculptory.tutorial.shapes.fill_cone: Selection > Fill fills exactly the cone's blocks.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.library.summar: Save what you built in the library, load it back and place it.
sculptory.tutorial.library.select: Press %s and select something you built.
sculptory.tutorial.library.open: Press %s to open the Library window (or File > Library…).
sculptory.tutorial.library.save: Click Save clipboard as…, type a name such as tutorial/my_build, and save it.
sculptory.tutorial.library.load: Click your build in the list, then Load: it becomes your clipboard.
sculptory.tutorial.library.place: Click Place (or double-click it), put the ghost down and press %s.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.flip.summary: Paste a copy turned upside down, and see what turns over and what stays.
sculptory.tutorial.flip.select: Press %s and select something with a top and a bottom: stairs, a roof, a door.
sculptory.tutorial.flip.paste: Press %s: a see-through copy follows the cursor.
sculptory.tutorial.flip.flip: Press %s: the ghost turns over inside its box. Stairs, slabs, doors and lanterns flip; torches, plants and beds can't, so they stay as they are and a message counts them.
sculptory.tutorial.flip.place: Click to drop it and press %s to place it.
sculptory.tutorial.flip.more: %s turns the ghost and %s mirrors it. Move and Stack take the flip too: a stack's copies turn over, each in its own box.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.export.summary: Write the clipboard as a .litematic, .schem or .nbt file, and bring files in.
sculptory.tutorial.export.copy: Press %s, select something and press %s to copy it.
sculptory.tutorial.export.open: File > Export… opens the export dialog (the Selection and Clipboard windows have an Export button too).
sculptory.tutorial.export.export: Type a name, pick .litematic under Format and click Export. The file goes to sculptory/exports in your game folder; .schem and .nbt work the same way.
sculptory.tutorial.export.import: To bring a file in, drag a .schem, .litematic or .nbt from your computer onto the game window while the editor is open: it becomes your clipboard, ready to place.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.build.summary: Build a road through points you click, pull a face out of a wall, and pour water.
sculptory.tutorial.build.generate_pick: Press %s for Generate. In Tool Settings it makes a Path (a road), a Roof or a Line.
sculptory.tutorial.build.nodes: Click the ground in a few places: the road's centre line runs through them.
sculptory.tutorial.build.road: Press %s to build the road. %s undoes the whole road.
sculptory.tutorial.build.extrude: Aim at a wall or a floor and drag away from it: the flat face is pulled out. Let go to build it.
sculptory.tutorial.build.fluid: Set Mode to Fluid ball and click the ground for a ball of water. Flood fills a hollow up to where you aim; Drain takes water away.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.scatter.summar: Spread plants, rocks or trees over an area, preview them, and commit.
sculptory.tutorial.scatter.mix: Add something to scatter: %s a flower or a plant in the world, or click + Block or + Tree in Tool Settings.
sculptory.tutorial.scatter.area: Left-drag on the ground to paint the area (Alt+drag erases from it; Alt+click places one thing right there).
sculptory.tutorial.scatter.preview: In a moment, ghosts show where things will go. Change Density or the Seed (Random) to try another layout.
sculptory.tutorial.scatter.commit: Press %s to scatter them: one edit, one undo step.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.tinker.summary: Change one block's properties where it stands: scroll a value, pick a property, open the panel.
sculptory.tutorial.tinker.pick: Press %s for Tinker: it changes one block where it stands, without block updates.
sculptory.tutorial.tinker.aim: Point at a block with properties, stairs say. Beside the cursor: its name and one property, such as shape.
sculptory.tutorial.tinker.scroll: Scroll to move that property to its next value (Shift+Scroll picks another property). Each notch is one undo step.
sculptory.tutorial.tinker.panel: Click the block: its panel opens with every property as a drop-down.
sculptory.tutorial.tinker.change: Change a property in the panel. Apply to all like it in the selection sets it on every block of that kind you selected.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.builder.summar: Build in normal play with powers from the G ring, undo included.
sculptory.tutorial.builder.intro: Builder mode is Sculptory in normal play: with a power on, every block you place or break is one step of the same history. It needs Creative and the builder permission.
sculptory.tutorial.builder.power: Press %s to leave the editor. Hold %s: a ring of powers opens; let go on Place in air. Then press %s to come back here.
sculptory.tutorial.builder.place_undo: Press %s to leave, aim at the sky and right-click: the block in your hand lands 5 blocks ahead. %s takes it back (%s puts it back). Come back.
sculptory.tutorial.builder.off: Leave once more and tap %s: the last power you touched switches off and its tag above the hotbar goes. Press %s to come back.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.history.summar: Undo, redo, and jump back through your history.
sculptory.tutorial.history.change: Make any change: press %s and drag on the ground, say.
sculptory.tutorial.history.window: Press %s to open the History window: your steps, each named by its tool, around ▶ Now.
sculptory.tutorial.history.jump: Click a step below ▶ Now to go back to it, or one above to go forward again.
sculptory.tutorial.history.anyway: Undo leaves alone blocks that someone or something else changed since your edit. When it kept some, a toast offers Undo anyway.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.symmetry.summa: Mirror every brush dab around a centre you set.
sculptory.tutorial.symmetry.mode: Open the Symmetry section in Tool Settings and set Repeat each dab to Mirror east / west.
sculptory.tutorial.symmetry.centre: Point at the ground and press %s: the symmetry centre goes there (%s on the same spot clears it).
sculptory.tutorial.symmetry.stroke: Drag on one side of the line: the other side follows.
sculptory.tutorial.symmetry.others: Every brush, Select, Place, Extrude and Fluid have a Symmetry section too, around the same centre.
sculptory.tutorial.symmetry.off: Set Repeat each dab back to Off.
sculptory.tutorial.lesson.settings.summa: Tool Settings, typed values, presets, your own keys and the editor's size.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.hover: Hover any setting in Tool Settings to see what it does.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.change: Change a setting: drag a slider, or double-click it, type a value and press Enter.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.reset: A changed setting shows ↺ at its right: click it to go back to the default.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.preset: Presets keep all of a tool's settings: click Save as… at the top of Tool Settings and give it a name.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.keys: Help > Change keys… lists every key: click one, then press the new key.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.ui_size: Make the editor smaller or larger with %s and %s, or with the UI size button in the top bar.
sculptory.tutorial.settings.done: %s puts the size back to 100%%. The wiki has every window and setting.
sculptory.notifications.empty: No messages yet. Every message the editor shows at the top right is kept here (the last 100).
sculptory.notifications.count.tooltip: The last %s messages are kept, until you leave the game
sculptory.wiki.back.tooltip: Back: the page you were on before (also Backspace or Alt+Left on the page, and the mouse's back button)
sculptory.wiki.forward.tooltip: Forward: the page you went back from (also Alt+Right on the page, and the mouse's forward button)
sculptory.wiki.home.tooltip: Home: the wiki's front page, with every page by what you want to do
sculptory.wiki.pages.tooltip: Every page, and a search of their titles and headings
sculptory.wiki.no_matches: No page title or heading has those words.
sculptory.wiki.no_pages: This copy of the mod has no wiki pages.
sculptory.wiki.picture.tooltip: Click to see it full size
sculptory.wiki.picture.close: Click or press Esc to close
sculptory.wiki.tool_help.tooltip: This tool's page in the wiki
sculptory.notice.no_window_to_focus: No open window has a control to move the keyboard to
sculptory.library.add_to_scatter.tooltip: Add the asset to the Scatter tool's mix (tool 9)
sculptory.hint.scatter.add_block: add the block to the mix
sculptory.hint.scatter.add_variants: Add variants: Library (L) → Add to scatter, Add clipboard, + Block, or drop a .schem, .litematic or .nbt file
sculptory.setting.scatter.radius.tooltip: The radius of the brush you paint the area with, 1 to 64 blocks. Ctrl+Scroll changes it (Shift: steps of 4). The area already painted stays as it is.
sculptory.setting.scatter.seed.tooltip: Fixes every random choice: which columns get a placement, which variant and which turn. The same seed, settings and terrain give the same scatter. Random picks a new one.
sculptory.setting.scatter.density_mode.t: How many placements to try: a percentage of the suitable columns, or a target count.
sculptory.setting.scatter.density_mode.p: A share of the columns that pass the filters is tried, spread over the whole area.
sculptory.setting.scatter.density_mode.c: Columns are tried in a random order until the target count is placed, or the area runs out of room.
sculptory.setting.scatter.density.toolti: The share of the columns that pass the filters that are tried, 0.1 to 100%%. Spacing, fit and overlaps remove some, so usually fewer are placed.
sculptory.setting.scatter.count.tooltip: How many placements to aim for, 1 to 131,072. Columns are tried in a random order until this many are placed; with too little room you get fewer.
sculptory.setting.scatter.spacing.toolti: The least horizontal distance between two placements' anchor blocks, 0 to 64 blocks. Placements never overlap, even at 0.
sculptory.setting.scatter.filter.slope.t: Place only where the steepest step from the surface to a neighbouring column (north, south, east or west) is in this range, in blocks. The full range, 0 to 16, means no limit.
sculptory.setting.scatter.filter.elevati: Place only where the surface a placement stands on lies in this Y range (the seabed or the water surface for water plants). The full range, -64 to 319, means no limit.
sculptory.setting.scatter.filter.substra: Place only on these blocks: the block a placement stands on (the seabed for underwater plants, water for lily pads). Up to 16; empty: any block.
sculptory.setting.scatter.turn.0.tooltip: Placements may keep the orientation they were saved in. Each placement picks one of the ticked turns; with none ticked, all keep their orientation.
sculptory.setting.scatter.turn.90.toolti: Placements may be turned 90° clockwise. Each picks one of the ticked turns, from the seed; an asset that allows only some turns keeps to those.
sculptory.setting.scatter.turn.180.toolt: Placements may be turned 180°. Each picks one of the ticked turns, from the seed; an asset that allows only some turns keeps to those.
sculptory.setting.scatter.turn.270.toolt: Placements may be turned 270° clockwise (90° counterclockwise). Each picks one of the ticked turns, from the seed; an asset that allows only some turns keeps to those.
sculptory.setting.scatter.mirror.tooltip: Placements may also be mirrored: each picks, from the seed, one of the ticked turns, as it is or mirrored. Turns and mirroring together give every orientation.
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.survive.to: Single-block variants go only where the game lets the block stay: flowers on grass or dirt, cactus on sand. Assets and clipboards are not affected.
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.fluid: Allow in water and other fluids
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.fluid.tool: Assets and clipboards: on, they may replace water and waterlogged blocks (a reef); off, water blocks them. Underwater plants: on, they may replace water plants already there.
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.support.to: How much of a variant's lowest layer needs ground right under it, 0 to 100%%; the rest may hang over air. The column it is anchored on always needs ground.
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.column: Column height (sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp)
sculptory.setting.scatter.fit.column.too: How tall sugar cane, cactus, bamboo and kelp grow, 1 to 32 blocks: each picks a height in this range, cut to the room above it. A spot with less room than the minimum is skipped.
sculptory.scatter.panel.use_selection.to: Scatter over the whole selection box instead of a painted area (a shaped or block selection counts as the box around it)
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_clipboard.to: Add the current clipboard to the mix
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_block.toolti: Add a single block (a flower, grass, a plant, seagrass, kelp, coral, a lily pad) to the mix. Water plants go under water, lily pads on water. Tip: middle-click a block in the world
sculptory.scatter.panel.underwater.toolt: Placed on the ground under still water, every block in still water (seagrass, kelp, coral, sea pickles and waterlogged blocks)
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_block.no_per: Adding single blocks needs the brush or region permission — ask an operator
sculptory.scatter.panel.hint: Add library assets with the Library's Add to scatter (L), drop a .schem, .litematic or .nbt file on the editor, or add single blocks with + Block or a middle-click in the world.
sculptory.scatter.panel.area_empty: Area: none yet — paint on the terrain (LMB drag)
sculptory.scatter.panel.weight: Weight (1-1000): how often this variant is picked
sculptory.scatter.panel.replaced.tooltip: The server keeps one clipboard, and this one was replaced by a newer copy. Remove it, or add the clipboard again.
sculptory.scatter.panel.failed.tooltip: Its preview couldn't be loaded — press R to try again
sculptory.scatter.panel.block_unknown.to: This game doesn't have that block (a mod that isn't installed?). It is left out of the preview
sculptory.scatter.status.no_area: Paint an area on the terrain (LMB drag), or use the selection
sculptory.scatter.status.no_variants: Add a variant to preview: Library (L) → Add to scatter, Add clipboard, or + Block
sculptory.scatter.status.no_usable_varia: None of the variants can be used right now (see Tool Settings)
sculptory.scatter.status.stale: Preview is out of date — adjust or press %s to refresh
sculptory.scatter.status.failed: The preview didn't arrive — press %s to try again
sculptory.scatter.status.refused.area_bu: The area is still busy with another edit — press %s once it has finished
sculptory.scatter.status.refused.rate_li: The server needs a moment before the next preview — press %s to try again
sculptory.scatter.status.lod: Nearest %s shown as ghosts, %s more as outlines and dots
sculptory.notice.scatter_added: Added %s to the scatter mix (%s variants)
sculptory.notice.scatter_clipboard_repla: Added %s to the scatter mix, replacing the older clipboard
sculptory.notice.scatter_duplicate: %s is already in the scatter mix
sculptory.notice.scatter_block_permissio: Single blocks as scatter variants need the %s or %s permission — use clipboards or library assets instead
sculptory.notice.scatter_mix_full: The scatter mix is full (%s variants)
sculptory.notice.scatter_area_full: The area is full (%s stamps) — undo, erase or clear to paint more
sculptory.notice.scatter_area_too_wide: A scatter area can't span more than %s columns
sculptory.notice.scatter_planning: The preview is still being made — press Enter again when it shows
sculptory.notice.scatter_paint_first: Paint an area first (LMB drag on the terrain)
sculptory.notice.scatter_add_variant: Add a variant first: Library (L) → Add to scatter
sculptory.notice.scatter_no_preview: No preview yet — press %s to make one
sculptory.notice.scatter_expired: The preview expired — making a new one; press Enter again when it shows
sculptory.notice.scatter_nothing: Nothing to place: no column passed the filters
sculptory.notice.scatter_commit_invalid: The server no longer has that preview (it expired or was replaced) — press %s for a new one
sculptory.notice.scatter_commit_no_permi: You may not scatter here, can no longer read one of the library assets in the mix, or may no longer use single blocks as variants
sculptory.notice.scatter_finished_skippe: Scatter done: %s blocks placed · %s placements skipped or left incomplete (built on, protected or not loaded)
sculptory.notice.scatter_protected: Scatter: %s blocks were left alone because they are protected
sculptory.notice.scatter_skipped: Scatter: %s placements were skipped or left incomplete (built on, protected or not loaded)
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_tree.tooltip: Add a vanilla tree to the mix (oak, big oak, birch, spruce, jungle, acacia, dark oak, cherry, mangrove, azalea, huge mushrooms…). Each spot grows its own tree, exactly as the preview shows; Re-roll grows others
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_feature.tool: Add a vanilla feature to the mix (a mossy boulder, an ice spike, a moss patch, flower, grass and berry patches…). Each spot grows its own, exactly as the preview shows
sculptory.scatter.panel.add_feature.no_p: Trees and features need the brush or region permission — ask an operator
sculptory.scatter.panel.tree.tooltip: Grown by the game at each spot, as in world generation: only where its sapling could stand while "only where it can survive" is on, and never turned
sculptory.scatter.panel.feature.tooltip: Grown by the game at each spot, as in world generation; where it doesn't grow (an ice spike off snow), the spot is counted as "didn't grow"
sculptory.notice.scatter_feature_permiss: Trees and features as scatter variants need the %s or %s permission — use clipboards or library assets instead
sculptory.notice.scatter_one_miss: Point at the terrain to place one
sculptory.notice.scatter_one_failed: Placing one didn't work — try again
sculptory.scatter.feature.fancy_oak_bees: Big oak with a bee nest
